```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Dissanayake 2018 fitted two one-compartment oral population PK models to the
first-dose metformin profiles of 18 metformin-naive patients with type 2
diabetes and chronic kidney disease stage 4. The library carries both:

* `Dissanayake_2018_metformin`: Equation (1), parameterised by K, ka and
  CL/F, with no covariates (Table 2). AIC and BIC preferred this model.
* `Dissanayake_2018_metformin_crcl`: Equation (2), in which CL/F is baseline
  creatinine clearance (in L/h) times an estimated ratio (Table A3). The
  authors used this model for the CrCl-specific dose recommendations of
  Table A4.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dissanayake_2018_metformin"))$reference`
* Description (no CrCl): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dissanayake_2018_metformin"))$description`
* Description (CrCl): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dissanayake_2018_metformin_crcl"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.424>

# Population

Eighteen metformin-naive adults with type 2 diabetes (diagnosed at least two
years earlier, HbA1c 6-11%) and CKD stage 4 (eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m^2, not
on dialysis) took part in a New Zealand Phase I open-label consecutive-cohort
dose-escalation study. Six patients each received immediate-release metformin
hydrochloride 250, 500 or 1000 mg once daily for about four weeks. Median age
was 66.0 years and median BMI 38.0 kg/m^2 (every patient had BMI >= 23);
4 of 18 were female. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance on adjusted body
weight ranged 18-49 mL/min (median 30.2). Serum metformin was sampled at 0, 2,
4, 6, 8 and 24 h after the first dose (102 concentrations), and fasting
troughs at later visits. Both PK models were fitted to the first-dose profiles
only, with R `nlme` (Results text; Table A1).

The same information is available programmatically through the `population`
element of each model, e.g.
`readModelDb("Dissanayake_2018_metformin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Structure: first-order absorption into one compartment, `c(t) = D K ka / (CL/F (ka - K)) (exp(-K t) - exp(-ka t))` | n/a | Equation (1), Methods 'Pharmacokinetics: single-dose hourly concentrations' |
| `lka_int` (no CrCl) | log(0.65) 1/h | Table 2, ka |
| `lcl_int` (no CrCl) | log(29.6) L/h | Table 2, Cl/F |
| `lkel` (no CrCl) | log(0.119) 1/h | Table 2, K |
| `vc = cl / kel` | 248.7 L typical | Table 2 derives V/F = 249.7 L from the same estimates |
| `etacl`, `etaka` (no CrCl) | var 133.6336, 0.156025; cov 3.584467 | Table 2, sd(Cl/F) 11.56 L/h, sd(ka) 0.395 1/h, cor 0.785 |
| `addSd` (no CrCl) | 0.095 mg/L | Table 2, Resid. SE |
| Structure: CL/F = CrCl (L/h) x (Cl/F)' | n/a | Equation (2) |
| `lka_int` (CrCl) | log(0.564) 1/h | Table A3, ka |
| `lkel` (CrCl) | log(0.128) 1/h | Table A3, K |
| `e_crcl_cl` (CrCl) | 17.4 | Table A3, Cl/F'; Results 'Pharmacokinetics and kidney function' |
| `etae_crcl_cl`, `etaka` (CrCl) | var 60.9961, 0.0961; cov 1.912669 | Table A3, sd(Cl/F') 7.81, sd(ka) 0.31 1/h, cor 0.79 |
| `addSd` (CrCl) | 0.099 mg/L | Table A3, Resid. SE printed 0.99 with 95% CI (0.08, 0.12) |
| `CRCL` | mL/min, converted to L/h in `model()` | Methods 'Other measures'; Table A1 adjusted-body-weight column |

# Typical-value replication of the published tables

Every number in Tables 2, 3, A3 and A4 is a typical-value quantity: it is
derived from the fixed effects alone (Table 2 footnote a). The chunks below
solve each model with its random effects removed and compare against the
printed values. These are deterministic solves, so the bounds only need to
admit the rounding of the printed estimates.

```{r typical-helpers}
mod1 <- readModelDb("Dissanayake_2018_metformin")
mod2 <- readModelDb("Dissanayake_2018_metformin_crcl")
mod1_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod1)
mod2_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod2)

single_dose_typical <- function(mod, dose, crcl = NULL) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame()
  if (!is.null(crcl)) ev$CRCL <- crcl
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
    maxsteps = 1e6
  )
  data.frame(dose = dose, cmax = max(s$Cc), tmax = s$time[which.max(s$Cc)])
}

# Once-daily dosing for 30 days; the last interval is at steady state (t1/2
# about 6 h). maxsteps is raised because liblsoda charges its step budget
# across the whole 30-day run at these tolerances.
steady_state_typical <- function(mod, dose, crcl = NULL) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, cmt = "depot", ii = 24, addl = 29) |>
    rxode2::et(seq(696, 720, by = 0.01), cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame()
  if (!is.null(crcl)) ev$CRCL <- crcl
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame", rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12,
    maxsteps = 1e6
  )
  s <- s[s$time >= 696, ]
  data.frame(
    dose = dose,
    cmin_ss = s$Cc[nrow(s)],
    cavg_ss = mean(s$Cc),
    cmax_ss = max(s$Cc)
  )
}
```

## Table 2: single-dose Cmax, tmax and AUC (model without CrCl)

```{r table2}
tab2 <- bind_rows(lapply(c(250, 500, 1000), single_dose_typical, mod = mod1_typ)) |>
  mutate(aucinf = dose / 29.6) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~dose, ~cmax_pub, ~tmax_pub, ~aucinf_pub,
      250,   0.69,      3.19,      8.43,
      500,   1.37,      3.19,      16.87,
      1000,  2.74,      3.19,      33.74
    ),
    by = "dose"
  )
tab2 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose,
    "Cmax model (mg/L)" = cmax, "Cmax Table 2" = cmax_pub,
    "tmax model (h)" = tmax, "tmax Table 2" = tmax_pub,
    "AUC0-inf = D/(CL/F) (mg*h/L)" = aucinf, "AUC0-inf Table 2" = aucinf_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value single-dose exposure versus Table 2.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(tab2) == 3,
  all(abs(tab2$cmax / tab2$cmax_pub - 1) < 0.01),
  all(abs(tab2$tmax - tab2$tmax_pub) < 0.02),
  # Table 2's AUC carries the unrounded CL/F; 29.6 L/h reproduces it to 0.2%.
  all(abs(tab2$aucinf / tab2$aucinf_pub - 1) < 0.005)
)
```

## Table 3: steady-state concentrations (model without CrCl)

```{r table3}
tab3 <- bind_rows(lapply(c(250, 500, 1000), steady_state_typical, mod = mod1_typ)) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~dose, ~cmin_pub, ~cavg_pub, ~cmax_pub,
      250,   0.08,      0.35,      0.74,
      500,   0.15,      0.70,      1.47,
      1000,  0.30,      1.41,      2.95
    ),
    by = "dose"
  )
tab3 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg/day)" = dose,
    "Cmin,ss model" = cmin_ss, "Cmin,ss Table 3" = cmin_pub,
    "Cavg,ss model" = cavg_ss, "Cavg,ss Table 3" = cavg_pub,
    "Cmax,ss model" = cmax_ss, "Cmax,ss Table 3" = cmax_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value steady state (mg/L) versus Table 3.")

# Table 3 prints two decimals; the bound admits half a unit in the last place
# plus the rounding of the three printed estimates.
stopifnot(
  nrow(tab3) == 3,
  all(abs(tab3$cmin_ss - tab3$cmin_pub) <= 0.006),
  all(abs(tab3$cavg_ss - tab3$cavg_pub) <= 0.006),
  all(abs(tab3$cmax_ss - tab3$cmax_pub) <= 0.011)
)
```

## Tables A3 and A4: the CrCl model

Table A3 gives tmax = 3.40 h for this model. Table A4 gives steady-state
concentrations at baseline creatinine clearances of 30-50 mL/min, which fixes
both the L/h unit of CrCl in Equation (2) and the reading of the 17.4 ratio:
at 30 mL/min (1.8 L/h), CL/F = 31.3 L/h and Cavg,ss for 1000 mg is
1000 / (31.3 x 24) = 1.33 mg/L, as printed.

```{r tableA4}
tA3 <- single_dose_typical(mod2_typ, 1000, crcl = 30)
stopifnot(abs(tA3$tmax - 3.40) < 0.02)

grid <- expand.grid(crcl = c(30, 35, 40, 45, 50), dose = c(250, 500, 1000))
tabA4 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(i) {
  steady_state_typical(mod2_typ, grid$dose[i], crcl = grid$crcl[i]) |>
    mutate(crcl = grid$crcl[i])
})) |>
  left_join(
    tibble::tribble(
      ~crcl, ~dose, ~cmin_pub, ~cavg_pub, ~cmax_pub,
      30, 250, 0.06, 0.33, 0.70,
      35, 250, 0.06, 0.28, 0.60,
      40, 250, 0.05, 0.25, 0.53,
      45, 250, 0.04, 0.22, 0.47,
      50, 250, 0.04, 0.20, 0.42,
      30, 500, 0.13, 0.66, 1.40,
      35, 500, 0.11, 0.57, 1.20,
      40, 500, 0.10, 0.50, 1.05,
      45, 500, 0.09, 0.44, 0.94,
      50, 500, 0.08, 0.40, 0.84,
      30, 1000, 0.26, 1.33, 2.81,
      35, 1000, 0.22, 1.14, 2.40,
      40, 1000, 0.19, 1.00, 2.10,
      45, 1000, 0.17, 0.89, 1.87,
      50, 1000, 0.15, 0.80, 1.68
    ),
    by = c("crcl", "dose")
  )
stopifnot(nrow(tabA4) == 15, !anyNA(tabA4$cmax_pub))

tabA4 |>
  select(crcl, dose, cmin_ss, cmin_pub, cavg_ss, cavg_pub, cmax_ss, cmax_pub) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CrCl (mL/min)" = crcl, "Dose (mg)" = dose,
    "Cmin,ss model" = cmin_ss, "Cmin,ss Table A4" = cmin_pub,
    "Cavg,ss model" = cavg_ss, "Cavg,ss Table A4" = cavg_pub,
    "Cmax,ss model" = cmax_ss, "Cmax,ss Table A4" = cmax_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value steady state (mg/L) for the CrCl model versus Table A4.")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(tabA4$cmin_ss - tabA4$cmin_pub) <= 0.006),
  all(abs(tabA4$cavg_ss - tabA4$cavg_pub) <= 0.006),
  all(abs(tabA4$cmax_ss - tabA4$cmax_pub) <= 0.011)
)
```

All 45 Table A4 cells and all of Tables 2 and 3 are reproduced to within the
printed rounding.

# Virtual cohort

The random effects in both models are additive and normal on the natural
parameter scale (the paper reports sd(Cl/F) in L/h and sd(ka) in 1/h). Taken
literally, that distribution gives about 5% of subjects a negative ka in the
model without CrCl (0.65 / 0.395 = 1.65 SD). The cohort below therefore draws
the random effects in R from the published covariance matrix and redraws any
subject with a non-positive ka or CL/F before passing them to `rxSolve()`.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(6138239)

draw_positive_etas <- function(n, omega, typical) {
  out <- matrix(numeric(0), ncol = ncol(omega), dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(omega)))
  while (nrow(out) < n) {
    z <- matrix(stats::rnorm(n * ncol(omega)), ncol = ncol(omega)) %*% chol(omega)
    colnames(z) <- colnames(omega)
    keep <- apply(sweep(z, 2, typical, "+") > 0, 1, all)
    out <- rbind(out, z[keep, , drop = FALSE])
  }
  out[seq_len(n), , drop = FALSE]
}

n_per_arm <- 200L
doses <- c(250, 500, 1000)
omega1 <- rxode2::rxode2(mod1)$omega
etas1 <- draw_positive_etas(
  n_per_arm * length(doses), omega1,
  typical = c(etacl = 29.6, etaka = 0.65)[colnames(omega1)]
)
subjects <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_per_arm * length(doses)),
  dose = rep(doses, each = n_per_arm)
) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose, "mg"))
params1 <- bind_cols(subjects |> select(id), as.data.frame(etas1))

# First-dose profile (dense, 0-72 h) for NCA, then once-daily dosing to day 28
# with a trough 24 h after every dose.
obs_sd <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(13, 72, by = 1))))
events1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(subjects)), function(i) {
  s <- subjects[i, ]
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = s$id, time = 0, amt = s$dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = 0, addl = 0),
    tibble(id = s$id, time = obs_sd, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = s$treatment, phase = "single")
}))
events_md <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(subjects)), function(i) {
  s <- subjects[i, ]
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = s$id, time = 0, amt = s$dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", ii = 24, addl = 27),
    tibble(id = s$id, time = 24 * (1:28), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", ii = 0, addl = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(treatment = s$treatment, phase = "repeat")
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events1[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

`rxSolve()` warns that a multi-subject simulation has no `omega` when every
subject's random effects are supplied through `params`; that is the intent
here, so only that warning is muffled.

```{r simulate}
muffle_no_omega <- function(expr) {
  withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
      invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  })
}
sim_sd <- muffle_no_omega(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod1, events = events1, params = params1, keep = "treatment",
  returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6
))
sim_md <- muffle_no_omega(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod1, events = events_md, params = params1, keep = "treatment",
  returnType = "data.frame", maxsteps = 1e6
))
# The supplied random effects reach the solve: the individual CL/F match the draws.
chk <- sim_sd |> distinct(id, cl) |> left_join(params1, by = "id")
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$cl - (29.6 + chk$etacl))) < 1e-6)
```

## Single-dose profiles

```{r single-dose-vpc, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
sim_sd |>
  filter(time <= 24) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = paste(doses, "mg"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Serum metformin (mg/L)",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles, 200 virtual patients per dose (model without CrCl)."
  )
```

## Repeat-dose troughs (Figure 1)

Figure 1 overlays observed troughs on the steady-state minimum, average and
maximum concentrations implied by the model. The dashed lines below are those
typical values (Table 3); the ribbon is the 5th-95th percentile of the
simulated troughs, i.e. the between-patient spread the model itself predicts.

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
ss_lines <- tab3 |>
  transmute(treatment = paste(dose, "mg"), Cmin = cmin_ss, Cavg = cavg_ss, Cmax = cmax_ss) |>
  pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = paste(doses, "mg")))
sim_md |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = paste(doses, "mg"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(data = ss_lines, aes(yintercept = conc, linetype = quantity)) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Days after first dose", y = "Serum metformin (mg/L)", linetype = "Typical steady state",
    caption = "Replicates the model bands of Figure 1 of Dissanayake 2018 (observed troughs not reproduced)."
  )
```

The paper's observed troughs were consistently above the modelled minimum in
the 11 patients whose creatinine clearance was below about 32 mL/min
(Figure 2), and within it in the 7 patients with higher clearance
(Figure 3). The authors conclude that this single-dose model under-predicts
accumulation in the lower half of the CKD-4 range; the model reproduces what
was fitted (24-h first-dose profiles) and should not be extrapolated to
long-term troughs below that clearance.

# PKNCA validation

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events1 |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published values

Table 2 reports model-based (typical-value) Cmax, tmax, AUC0-inf and
elimination half-life; the simulated column is the median over each virtual
dose arm.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  "250 mg",   0.69,  3.19,  8.43,        5.84,
  "500 mg",   1.37,  3.19,  16.87,       5.84,
  "1000 mg",  2.74,  3.19,  33.74,       5.84
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated (median of 200 per arm) versus Table 2. * differs by >20%.")

nca_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    published |> tidyr::pivot_longer(-treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub"),
    by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")
  )
stopifnot(nrow(nca_med) == 6, !anyNA(nca_med$pub))
# Cohort medians, not extremes: a mis-transcribed CL/F, ka or dose moves these
# by tens of percent, while redrawing the non-positive tail moves them by a
# few percent.
stopifnot(all(abs(nca_med$med / nca_med$pub - 1) < 0.10))
```

The medians sit close to the typical values because the random effects are
symmetric on the natural scale; the small upward shift in the median CL/F (and
so the slightly lower median AUC) comes from discarding the non-positive tail.

# The CrCl model in the study cohort

Table A1 lists each patient's baseline creatinine clearance. Solving the CrCl
model at its typical values for those 18 patients shows how strongly the
predicted steady-state trough depends on renal function within CKD stage 4.

```{r tableA1-cohort, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
tabA1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~patient, ~dose, ~CRCL,
  1, 250, 17.96, 2, 250, 23.43, 3, 250, 36.70, 4, 250, 31.24, 5, 250, 42.91, 6, 250, 26.18,
  7, 500, 24.46, 8, 500, 41.96, 9, 500, 23.96, 10, 500, 22.50, 11, 500, 48.55, 12, 500, 40.54,
  13, 1000, 31.05, 14, 1000, 27.84, 16, 1000, 31.73, 17, 1000, 27.08, 18, 1000, 21.87, 19, 1000, 23.15
)
stopifnot(nrow(tabA1) == 18, abs(median(tabA1$CRCL) - 27.46) < 0.01)

a1 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tabA1)), function(i) {
  steady_state_typical(mod2_typ, tabA1$dose[i], crcl = tabA1$CRCL[i]) |>
    mutate(patient = tabA1$patient[i], CRCL = tabA1$CRCL[i])
}))
ggplot(a1, aes(CRCL, cmin_ss, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 32, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Baseline CrCl, adjusted body weight (mL/min)", y = "Typical Cmin,ss (mg/L)",
    colour = "Dose (mg/day)",
    caption = "Dashed line: the 32 mL/min boundary below which observed troughs exceeded the model (Results)."
  )
```

At the cohort median CrCl the CrCl model's typical CL/F is close to the
model without CrCl, as expected from two fits to the same data:

```{r crcl-consistency}
cl_at_median <- 30.2 * 60 / 1000 * 17.4
cl_at_median
stopifnot(abs(cl_at_median / 29.6 - 1) < 0.1)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Sign of Equation (1).** Equations (1) and (2) print the denominator as
  `(K - ka)`; with the positive difference `exp(-K t) - exp(-ka t)` that
  gives negative concentrations whenever ka > K. The model uses the standard
  `(ka - K)`, which reproduces every Cmax, tmax and steady-state value the
  paper derives from these equations (Tables 2, 3, A3 and A4).
- **Residual error of the CrCl model.** Table A3 prints 'Resid. SE' = 0.99
  mg/L with a 95% CI of (0.08, 0.12). The point estimate lies outside its own
  interval and is ten times the 0.095 mg/L of the companion model fitted to
  the same data, so the maintainers read it as 0.099 mg/L.
- **Units of the CrCl coefficient.** Equation (2) takes CrCl in L/h
  (Methods). The model's `CRCL` column is in mL/min, the register's unit, and
  `model()` converts it; Table A4 is reproduced only with that conversion.
- **Random effects on the natural scale.** Both models were fitted with R
  `nlme`, and Tables 2 and A3 report the random-effect SDs in the units of the
  parameters, so the etas are additive (`cl = exp(lcl_int) + etacl`). K has no
  random effect, so V/F = (CL/F)/K varies with CL/F. A literal draw from that
  distribution includes non-positive ka (about 5%) and CL/F (about 0.5%); the
  virtual cohort above redraws those subjects. Simulations that sample etas
  through `rxSolve()` directly do not apply that restriction.
- **V/F.** Table 2 prints V/F = 249.7 L; 29.6 / 0.119 = 248.7 L. The model
  derives V/F from the two printed estimates; the 0.4% difference reflects
  the paper's unrounded estimates.
- **Dose units.** Doses are milligrams of metformin hydrochloride, as
  prescribed and as used in the paper's AUC and clearance calculations.
- **CrCl definition.** Modified Cockcroft-Gault with a BMI-selected weight;
  every study patient had BMI >= 23 kg/m^2, so the adjusted body weight
  IBW + 0.4 x (TBW - IBW) applied throughout (Table A1).
- **Observed data.** Individual concentrations are not published, so the
  observed troughs of Figures 1-3 are not overlaid.
- **Cohort median CrCl.** The Results text gives a median CrCl of 30.2 mL/min
  (IQR 8.6); the 18 adjusted-body-weight values of Table A1 have a median of
  27.46 mL/min. The model metadata quotes the text; the cohort section above
  uses the Table A1 values.
- **Errata.** Europe PMC lists no correction or erratum for this article,
  and none among the records citing it, as of 2026-11-25.
